name: Composite Stylometric Fingerprinting
description: Generates a unique, multi-dimensional statistical signature (a 'fingerprint') of a text by fusing dozens of micro-features, including n-gram frequencies, punctuation topologies, syntactic dependency depths, and vocabulary richness. Because commercial Large Language Models are heavily fine-tuned via RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback) to be 'helpful, harmless, and honest', they inadvertently adopt a monolithic, highly sanitized, and perfectly average writing style. This results in a highly predictable algorithmic fingerprint across different generation sessions. Human writers, conversely, possess highly idiosyncratic, inconsistent, and deeply personalized stylometric fingerprints.
mechanism: The algorithm parses the text and extracts a vast array of linguistic micro-metrics, creating a high-dimensional vector representation of the document's style. It utilizes techniques similar to 'Winnowing' (Schleimer et al., 2003) to select robust, invariant hashes from these vectors. This composite fingerprint is then compared against a massive database of known AI generator signatures and standard human corpora. If the extracted fingerprint aligns closely with the generic, sanitized vector space of commercial LLMs, it is flagged as synthetic.
useCase: Highly effective for corporate and academic environments where identifying the precise origin or detecting 'copy-paste' AI boilerplates across multiple documents is necessary.
strengths:
• Extremely difficult to bypass, as altering one micro-feature (e.g., swapping a few adjectives) does not meaningfully change the underlying multi-dimensional syntactic fingerprint.
• Can often classify not just 'AI vs. Human', but potentially identify the specific model family (e.g., GPT-4 vs. Claude) based on its unique alignment signature.
limitations:
• Susceptible to 'false negatives' if the user heavily edits the text or applies an aggressive 'stylometric cloaking' prompt (e.g., 'write in the style of Edgar Allan Poe').
• Requires a substantial text length to develop a stable, high-confidence composite fingerprint, otherwise the hash becomes noisy.
parameters:
Analysis: High-Dimensional Stylometric Vector Fusing
Metric: Micro-Feature Hash Similarity to Known AI Baselines
Output: 0-100 Algorithmic Fingerprint Match Score
accuracy: High — 83-89% accuracy on medium to long texts. Acts as a highly reliable 'final verdict' metric when correlated with simpler statistical tests like perplexity.

references.title: Schleimer, S. et al. (2003). Winnowing: Local Algorithms for Document Fingerprinting. SIGMOD.
Potthast, M. et al. (2014). Overview of the 6th Plagiarism Detection Competition. CLEF.
